Where the Hardin County Clerk is and what it holds

The clerk works from Suite 103 of the Hardin County Government Building, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701, phone 270-765-2171. Doors are open weekdays from 7:45 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon. A branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd in Radcliff handles vehicle registrations Tuesday through Thursday from 8 to 4, but deeds go to Elizabethtown.

This office keeps deeds, mortgages, wills, plats, liens, assumed names and marriage records, and it also issues vehicle titles and tags and runs elections. A seller meets it three ways: when the deed to the buyer is recorded, when an old mortgage needs a release of record, and when a bill that missed the sheriff's April 15 cutoff has moved to the clerk.

Courthouse fires in 1864 and 1932 destroyed county records, so a title examiner working on a very old chain may find gaps that predate the present 1934 courthouse.

Searching land records online

The clerk's website runs an eSearch name search that works as a guest, and it indexes far more than deeds. Index types include deeds, mortgages, deeds of release, affidavits of descent, plats, powers of attorney, restrictions, wills, lis pendens, mechanics liens and ad valorem liens, along with fiscal court minutes and ordinances.

Two searches pay off before listing. A search on your own name should show the mortgage and, once paid, a deed of release. A search for liens should show nothing left unreleased, since a lien filed against a prior owner or a contractor can surface at a title company in the final week.

What a deed must contain to be accepted

The clerk must turn away a deed that breaks a content rule in KRS 382.135 or KRS 382.110. Title attorneys handle these items routinely, but a family transfer written from a form is where gaps show up.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for both parties.
  • The full price, backed by a notarized certificate signed by both sides. A gift deed carries a certificate saying so, with an estimated fair cash value.
  • An in-care-of address for the bill of the year of transfer.
  • The source of the grantor's title, by deed book and page when it came from a recorded deed, or a plain explanation when it came by inheritance.

An estate that passes land by will or intestacy adds one more filing: the personal representative lodges an affidavit listing who received each parcel and what it was valued at.

Recording fees

The clerk posts a fee schedule alongside its formatting rules. Paper should be white and unbound, in black ink, with no seals or highlighter and a three inch blank strip across the top of page one. Electronic filers use Simplifile, ePn or CSC.

Certified copy$5.00

Most documents add $3.00 for every page past five and $4.00 per extra reference, and a mortgage adds $3.00 per page past thirty. Confirm the total with the clerk before mailing a packet.

Transfer tax owed by the seller

The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 block of value, with any leftover amount counted as a full block, under KRS 142.050. The clerk works the figure out from the value stated in the deed, collects it before accepting the paper, and certifies the payment date and amount on the deed itself. The tax is collected once per transaction, in whichever county the deed is filed. The clerk keeps 5 percent for the work, and the rest goes to the county treasurer every three months for the general fund.

Exemptions include foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, transfers between spouses in a divorce, partitions, and parent to child gifts with only nominal consideration. When a deed carries no stated price, the tax is figured on the open market estimate.

When a deed is rejected or filed late

The statute bars the clerk from lodging a deed that fails the content rules, so a rejected package usually means a corrected deed, a new notarization and a second trip. A deed recorded in error still counts as notice to later buyers and creditors, but the defect can draw questions from a title insurer.

Timing rules apply to some transfers. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the clerk within 45 days of signing. A grantee under a deed from a court-appointed commissioner has five business days from receipt to file. If you are the seller on either kind of transfer, confirm with the other side that the deed has been filed before you consider the matter closed.

Other filings a seller may need

Selling often trips over small filings. These come up most often, with the clerk's charges.

  • Release of a paid mortgage: $46.00.
  • Affidavit of descent and distribution after an inheritance: $50.00.
  • Power of attorney: $50.00, and a revocation: $46.00.
  • Release of a mechanics lien: $46.00, or $60.00 for a bond that releases it.
  • Release of a judgment lien or federal tax lien: $46.00. A state tax lien release costs $5.00.
  • City lien and city release: $23.00.
  • Notary service at the counter: $5.00 per acknowledgement plus $2.00 per notarization.

None of these replaces a title search, but ordering them early prevents the delay of a lender waiting on a release.

Unpaid property tax and the clerk

Sellers with a delinquent bill from a prior year get the payoff from the clerk. After April 15 a bill is a certificate of delinquency in the clerk's office, and the clerk's page offers a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information. The recording schedule also lists $30.00 to record a certificate assignment and $46.00 for a reassignment or release.

Request a payoff in writing, dated near the closing date, because interest accrues monthly. If a third party bought the certificate, the payoff goes to that buyer. The closing agent can pay it from the sale proceeds, and a cash buyer who closes quickly leaves less time for interest to grow.

Hardin County market notes

Hardin County has 44,622 households averaging 2.44 people each, and median gross rent is $971. With Fort Knox in the county, some sellers and buyers work to a fixed report date, so a deed that meets every content rule on the first attempt avoids a trip back to Suite 103.

Before closing day, call 270-765-2171 and ask what the clerk will need from your side: the signed deed, the notarized price certificate, the payoff or release for any mortgage, and the money for transfer tax and recording. Having each piece ready the day before keeps a closing from stalling at the counter, and it gives you time to fix a missing signature or address.

Frequently asked questions

Can a deed be e-recorded in Hardin County, Kentucky?

Yes. The Hardin County Clerk lists Simplifile, ePn and CSC as accepted electronic recording vendors.

How much is a mortgage release at the Hardin County Clerk?

$46.00 for a full or partial release, plus $3.00 for each page past five. The deed itself is $50.00.

Who pays transfer tax on a Hardin County sale?

The seller, at fifty cents per $500 block of value, paid when the deed is filed. A leftover amount counts as a full block.

Does the Radcliff branch record deeds?

No. The Radcliff branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd handles vehicle registration on Tuesday through Thursday. Deeds are recorded at Suite 103, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown.

Is a state tax lien release cheaper than a federal one in Hardin County?

Yes. The clerk charges $5.00 to record a state tax lien or its release and $46.00 for a federal tax lien or release.

What the Warren County Clerk does for a home seller

When a Bowling Green house changes hands, the deed ends up in this office. The clerk handles elections, motor vehicles and public land records, plus marriage licenses, notary commissions and delinquent property taxes.

  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102.
  • Phone: (270) 842-9416. The fax for legal recordings is (270) 843-5319.
  • Doors open weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm.
  • The deed room is on the building's bottom floor, with public terminals and a deputy records clerk on hand to get you started.

Some errands belong elsewhere. Driver's licenses come from the state Transportation Cabinet, and traffic citations go to the Circuit Clerk at 1001 Center St., Suite 102.

Which county records a Kentucky deed?

The clerk where the land sits, or where most of a split parcel sits. That rule comes from KRS 382.110, which also bars a clerk from taking a deed that skips the seller's source of title. When the seller bought by a recorded deed, the new one cites that earlier deed's book, page and recording date. An heir states how and from whom the property came. A lender taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure has 45 days to file it.

What a deed must say before Warren County will file it

The contents come from KRS 382.135, and a deed lacking any item is refused. A deed from a title attorney normally covers all of them.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for the grantor and grantee.
  • The whole consideration paid.
  • A forwarding address for the tax bill of the year of transfer.
  • A sworn, notarized statement signed by both parties that the price on the deed is the whole price. A gift instead needs a statement saying so and estimating fair cash value.

When a house passes through an estate, the personal representative files a separate affidavit in every county with estate land, naming who gets what and its value. Clerk staff cannot do a title search or answer whether liens exist, so leave that to a title company.

For most documents a charge of $3.00 applies to each page beyond five. Mortgages and releases of mortgage work differently, adding $5.00 for each page beyond thirty.

Transfer tax at the counter

The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 of value, rounding any remainder up. KRS 142.050 makes the clerk do the math and take payment before accepting the deed. The clerk's cut is 5 percent, and the treasurer gets the remainder every quarter.

Value means the whole price including liens, or the estimated open market price for a gift. The statute exempts many ordinary transfers, such as foreclosure deeds, deeds that grant or release security for a debt, divorce transfers between spouses, partitions, tax sales, and nominal price deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild. Match your deed to the statute's wording before counting on an exemption.

How to look up land records

Two routes exist. You can sit at a terminal in the deed room, or you can use eCCLIX, a subscription service from a records vendor. Personal users get five free searches a day, and commercial users pay a subscription. Because the index follows party names and document types, an address search will not work. Look the owner up on the PVA's site first, then search the clerk's records by name.

Staff will point out how the system works but will not run the search for you. DocAlert is another service the clerk promotes. It is free and emails you when a mortgage or deed is filed under your name, which helps owners of vacant rentals or land spot fraud.

Unpaid property taxes

After April 15 the sheriff's open bills belong to the clerk. The office takes payments until its annual sale, runs a current list in PDF, and takes buyer registrations for the sale held at its East 10th Avenue office. Most outside buyers must also register with the state first, so the clerk sends them to the Department of Revenue's form. Call for a payoff before closing, because interest and commissions keep growing each month and the lien can travel with the land for 11 years.

Permits and other closing snags

Work done without a permit is where closings tend to snag. Warren County's Division for Building Services at 1141 State Street handles permits outside Bowling Green and Oakland and states that all new construction needs one. Sheds starting at 120 square feet, decks and pools need permits too, and the county's stormwater office generally bars fences, sheds, pools and additions inside a drainage easement without a written exception. Bowling Green has its own inspector at (270) 393-3615.

A farm with a long chain of title may have early records in Logan County rather than here, so ask the deed room where to look. Renters occupy 44.4 percent of homes in the county, and the median rent is $1,002, so many sellers are landlords. The median home value is $258,000.

Selling a house that needs work or owes tax

A tenant, a probate delay, half finished repairs or unpaid taxes need not hold up a sale, since a cash buyer will purchase as is. Line up the paperwork first: a payoff from the clerk for any delinquent bill, the sheriff's figure for the current year, and permit sign-offs for any work done on the house. Hand these to the closing attorney so the deed, the transfer tax and the payoffs all settle on one day.

Confirm that the deed you plan to sign cites how you took title and carries the mailing addresses and price statement described above. A deed that the clerk refuses can delay the closing, and a second trip to the recording counter costs time even when the fee is small.

Bring photo ID to the closing, and ask the closing attorney to confirm the clerk's current fee total before the day.

Frequently asked questions

Where is a deed recorded in Warren County?

At the Warren County Clerk's office, reached by mail at P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, or by phone at (270) 842-9416. Four e-recording vendors also send documents electronically.

How much does Warren County charge to record a deed?

The base fee is $50, with $3.00 added for each page past the fifth. A deed of correction costs $46. Transfer tax is extra, and the seller covers it.

Can I find a Warren County deed using only the address?

No. The clerk indexes by party names and document types. Find the owner by address on the PVA's website first, then search the clerk's index under that name.

Will clerk staff check my title?

No. Staff can demonstrate the index, yet they are not permitted to run a title search or declare a property free of liens. Hire a title company or attorney for that.

Where a Barren County deed gets recorded

The Barren County Clerk's office sits in the Barren County Government Center on the north side of the square, at 117 North Public Square, Suite 1A, Glasgow, KY 42141. The phone number is 270-651-3783. Every deed and mortgage on Barren County land is recorded there.

Under KRS 382.110 the filing belongs to the county that contains the land. A house in Cave City, Park City, Glasgow or near Barren River Lake is recorded in Glasgow, wherever the seller lives now. The same Legal Records Division collects delinquent real estate taxes, so back taxes on a house come up at this counter as well.

What else the clerk's office handles

Besides land records, the Glasgow office issues marriage licenses, notary commissions and going-out-of-business licenses. Its Motor Vehicle Division registers or renews more than 40,000 vehicles a year, collects county vehicle taxes including motorboats, issues decals, plates and disabled parking permits, and files liens on titled collateral. The Legal Records Division records and indexes every real estate document, among them powers of attorney, assignments, releases and UCC fixture filings.

One trip can cover several errands. A closing agent can bring the deed and a release in the same visit.

How much it costs to record a deed

The posted schedule took effect January 1, 2020, and the office points to KRS 64.012 and House Bill 537 as its basis. Pages beyond the fifth cost $3 each on most filings, while a mortgage waits until page thirty-one for that surcharge.

Why deeds get rejected

The clerk's recording page lists the usual reasons a filing comes back. Nearly all can be prevented, and a returned deed can push a closing back.

  • The document is not notarized, or the notary left off an expiration date or the date of notarization.
  • The filing fee is wrong or the check is unsigned.
  • The title source is incomplete, or there is no legal description of the property.
  • No in-care-of address appears for the tax bill.
  • The grantor or grantee mailing address is missing.
  • A copy was submitted where an original is required.
  • A power of attorney lacks two disinterested witnesses, a rule the clerk ties to KRS 457.050 effective July 15, 2018.

The in-care-of address and full-consideration requirements come from KRS 382.135, and the title source rule comes from KRS 382.110. Attorneys catch these routinely. If you drafted the deed yourself, go down the list line by line.

Transfer tax on a sale

The seller owes fifty cents for each $500 of value in the deed, and any leftover part of $500 is rounded up (KRS 142.050). The clerk figures the amount and holds the deed until it is paid.

The tax is paid at the counter when the deed is filed, so the closing agent normally deducts it from the seller's proceeds and brings the payment along with the fees. If the deed recites a price that looks unusually low for a sale between strangers, expect questions, since the tax is figured on the value stated.

No tax applies to a deed that only corrects an earlier deed, ties or frees a debt, follows a foreclosure, or passes between spouses, nor to a parent-child transfer for token consideration. For a gift, the base is market value.

Delinquent taxes and liens

After the sheriff's collection season closes, an unpaid bill becomes the clerk's concern, since the Legal Records Division collects delinquent real estate taxes. April 15 is the cutoff. The clerk then holds a certificate of delinquency, a lien goes on record, interest of 1 percent monthly begins, and fees for the county attorney and clerk follow.

KRS 134.015 sets December 31 as the due date, a 2 percent discount through November 1 and a 5 percent penalty in January. Because the balance grows monthly, get the clerk's payoff figure close to the closing date.

Online land records come through eCCLIX, sold by Software Management, LLC. A monthly account costs $200 to start, $65 monthly and $10 per extra user. A one-day account costs $45 to start and $15 for each 24 hours. Viewing at the clerk's office costs nothing.

DocAlert is a free email notice from the same vendor. It fires when a mortgage or deed is filed under a registered personal or business name. Landlords with several parcels, and heirs who live far away, can use it to spot a forged filing.

If you only need to look something up, such as the book and page of your own deed, free walk-in viewing is the cheapest route. Paid online access makes more sense for someone who searches often.

Closing agents who prefer not to visit the square can file electronically through CSC, Simplifile or ePN. Contact details for each vendor are on the clerk's recording page.

Barren County covers roughly 500 square miles of south-central Kentucky, and Glasgow is its largest city. The estimated 2025 population is 45,641, which is 2.6 percent above the April 2020 base. Half of owner-occupied houses are worth more than $178,000, and owners live in 65.2 percent of 18,017 households. There were 20,957 housing units as of July 2025. Middle household income is $50,628 and middle gross rent is $796.

Agriculture is the main industry, Glasgow is the manufacturing, medical and retail center, and Cave City lives on visitors to Mammoth Cave. Paperwork differs by parcel type. A farm may involve several tracts and an older plat, and a lodging lot near Cave City may carry easements. Each such document is recorded at the clerk at prices like those in the fee table. Three school systems cover the county, so buyers often ask which one serves a particular house.

Before closing, line these up

  • Locate the book and page of the deed you hold.
  • Check with the clerk for a recorded delinquency certificate or lien.
  • Get the address where the buyer wants the next tax bill sent.
  • Agree on who files the deed, electronically or in person in Glasgow.
  • For an inherited parcel, ask whether an affidavit of descent is needed. The clerk lists it at $50.

A deed's minimum is $50, plus $3 for every page beyond five. The $4 state tax on conveyances in KRS 142.010 may apply on top, so ask for a full total.

The clerk may return it. KRS 382.135 calls for an in-care-of address for that year's bill, and a missing address is on the clerk's rejection list.

The foot of the clerk's schedule prints the transfer tax as one dollar for every thousand dollars of value. The seller pays it, and the clerk collects it when the deed is handed in. On the low prices common here, it is usually a smaller line on the settlement statement than the title charges.

Foreclosure transfers, transfers between spouses and token-price family deeds may be exempt. If yours might qualify, ask the clerk before you sign. A deed cannot be accepted until the right amount is paid.

Usually a closing attorney or title agent carries in the signed deed, the notarized price certificate and a check for recording and transfer tax. Clerk staff compare the deed with the state's content rules, take the tax, stamp the date and amount on the deed and file it.

Expect a few small costs beyond the deed fee. If a mortgage is being paid off, its release lists at $46 and is recorded after closing. Add transfer tax and any page charges, and your closing agent can give you the real total.

  1. Gather the deed, the notarized oath and the payoff letter if there is a mortgage.
  2. Confirm the fee and the branch with the clerk.
  3. Pay recording and transfer tax when the deed is filed.
  4. Keep the stamped copy once it is returned.

Before you go to the clerk

A little preparation saves a second trip. Most delays at the counter come from a deed that fails the content rules or a check that does not cover everything.

  • Decide which office is closest. The Catlettsburg office is the seat, but Ashland sellers can use Carter Avenue.
  • Check that both parties' names and mailing addresses appear on the deed, along with the tax-bill address.

Possibly. Boyd County was formed in 1860 from parts of Greenup, Carter and Lawrence Counties, so a chain of title reaching back before that date can lead into the older counties' records. Title examiners follow the chain wherever it goes.

A second counter operates in Wilmore at 210 South Lexington Avenue, weekdays from 9 until 3. Call ahead to ask which services that branch handles before you carry a closing package there. Nicholasville is the seat and the largest city, which is why most sellers simply use the courthouse.

A house sale usually leaves three papers for the clerk: the deed to the buyer, the lender's payoff release, and sometimes an affidavit. The buyer's title agent expects all of them indexed before funds are released.

Bring these to the counter:

  • The signed, notarized deed with the sale price stated, because the deed tax is figured from that number.

  • The lender's release, if it has not been filed. The posted minimum for a release is $46.

A deed starts at $50 and a mortgage at $80. Phone ahead for the current total before writing a check.

Deed transfer tax

The seller owes 50 cents on each $500 of the price written in the deed, and a leftover amount counts as a full $500 block. The clerk collects it at the counter, and a deed isn't accepted for recording until it is paid. Only one county collects the tax on a sale, the one holding the land.

Two thirds of homes, 66.7 percent, are lived in by their owners. The median home value is $268,100, and households earn a median of $74,576. New subdivisions and former farm tracts keep the clerk's counter busy with plats, easements and survey references, each recorded as its own item with its own fee.

A seller's closing checklist

The Jessamine County Clerk. Go to the courthouse at 101 North Main Street in Nicholasville or call (859) 885-4161.

KRS 64.012 sets $33 for a short instrument, while the clerk's page starts a deed at $50. Check the current total with the clerk.

The seller. State law puts it on the grantor, 50 cents per $500 of stated value, collected by the clerk at filing.

Yes. The clerk offers DOCALERT, a free email alert for deeds and mortgages recorded under a registered personal or business name.

To June 30, 1966, for deeds, mortgages and wills. The indexes are free to view at the clerk's office, or by eCCLIX subscription from home.

Deeds go to the Graves County Clerk in Mayfield. Under KRS 382.110, an instrument has to be recorded where the land lies, or where most of the land lies if it straddles a county line. Filing anywhere else leaves the deed exposed to later buyers who had no notice of it and to creditors.

Real estate records are handled through the records vault, (270) 247-1697, while title transfers, marriage licenses and vehicle work go through (270) 247-1676.

That office also takes delinquent real estate tax, so one visit can cover an old balance and the new deed.

Recording fees

KRS 64.012 sets the schedule. It charges $33 to record and index a deed of up to five pages. A mortgage of up to 30 pages is $63. Each page past the limit adds $3, and the Clerk can also collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent storage of the record.

Of every $33 deed fee, the Clerk keeps $27 and $6 is sent to the state's affordable housing trust fund. A seller who needs the Clerk to notarize the deed should budget the $5 on top.

What a Kentucky deed must contain

KRS 382.135 forbids the Clerk from filing a deed that leaves out required items, so mistakes are stopped at the counter. The deed has to contain:

KRS 382.110 adds a lineage requirement. The deed must point to the grantor's own source of title, giving the office, book, page and recording date of the earlier deed. If the owner inherited the land, the deed says how and from whom.

Utility easement deeds, cemetery lot deeds, government rights-of-way and deeds that fix errors in an earlier deed are exempt from the price, tax-address and certificate items.

When an owner dies and the house passes by will or by the intestacy rules, the estate's personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk of every county holding estate land, ahead of closing the estate. It names the people receiving each parcel and the value assigned in handling the estate, or says no value was set.

A Graves County heir selling to a cash buyer should therefore expect two filings at the Clerk's office, the affidavit and the new deed, with the deed charged under the schedule above.

KRS 382.270 adds one more gate. A deed or mortgage does not protect against a buyer for value without notice, or against creditors, until it has been acknowledged or proved as the law directs.

Transfer tax for the seller

KRS 142.050 puts the tax on the grantor, meaning the seller, and the Clerk takes payment at the counter before filing the deed. Fifty cents buys each block of $500 in value, and a partial block counts as whole.

A paid-off mortgage is cleared with a release recorded at the Clerk's office. A seller whose lender never filed can discover the old mortgage still open on the record.

When a lender passes a mortgage to another holder, the new holder files the assignment within 30 days. Missing that deadline does not by itself affect the lien's validity.

A mortgage that keeps a lien in the deed also has to name the source of the borrower's title, and KRS 382.290 lets the Clerk charge the KRS 64.012 fee for each assignment and release noted on the record, paid by the person making the entry.

Ask the records vault before listing whether each earlier mortgage on the parcel shows as released. A paid loan that still shows as open is simpler to correct before a buyer's title search turns it up.

How to get a certified copy of a recorded deed

Ask the records vault. KRS 64.012 prices a certified copy at $5, with half a dollar added for every page past three. KRS 382.110 treats an authentic photocopy that the official custodian certifies as a true, unaltered copy of the original, and a certified copy can be filed in another county's office as if it were the original, provided it meets all the filing rules.

A certified copy helps when a parcel crosses a county line or when a lender wants proof of an earlier deed. Title agents sometimes want the last vesting deed in certified form.

  • Bring the grantor name, the approximate year and, if you have them, the deed book and page.
  • Ask whether the copy needs to carry the clerk's certification for out-of-county use.
  • Request a separate copy of any recorded release, so the chain from deed to payoff is complete.

Graves County housing and selling

Graves County sits in far western Kentucky, and Mayfield is the seat. Population is 37,050 across 14,139 households. Owners occupy 76.1 percent of homes, which have a median value of $147,800, and median gross rent is $775. A December 10, 2021 tornado caused major damage in Mayfield, including to the courthouse, and many properties changed hands or were rebuilt afterward, so clean recorded paperwork matters.

A seller who keeps the recorded paperwork in order, from the last vesting deed to the mortgage release, avoids the delays that title problems cause. A cash buyer purchasing as-is still needs the deed recorded the same way, but it can skip the lender's appraisal and repair demands.

Which office files deeds for a house in Graves County?

The Graves County Clerk, 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield. Call the records vault at (270) 247-1697 with questions about real estate filings.

Thirty-three dollars buys a recording of up to five pages, with $3 for each page beyond that and a $10 storage reimbursement. Transfer tax is charged separately.

Can the Clerk turn my deed away?

Yes. KRS 382.135 bars filing a deed that lacks names, addresses, the consideration statement, a tax-bill address or the sworn certificate, and the deed must also cite its source of title.

Is a mortgage release my lender's job or mine?

The lender or holder signs it, but it only counts once it is filed with the Clerk. Handing a copy to the borrower is not enough, so ask the records vault whether it appears on your parcel.

What do heirs file before selling an inherited Graves County house?

The personal representative lodges an affidavit at the Clerk's office naming each recipient and an estimated value, and the new deed follows. KRS 382.135 calls for it before the estate is closed.

Where a Laurel County deed gets recorded

Laurel County deeds go to the Laurel County Clerk. Its delinquent tax and records staff work from Room 203 at 101 S Main St in London (ZIP 40741), reachable at (606) 864-5158. KRS 382.110 places the filing in the county where the land lies. A parcel that crosses a county line is filed where most of it sits.

Sellers seldom handle the paper. The closing attorney or title agent brings the signed deed in, settles the charges at the counter and gets the recorded original back by mail. Recording matters because an unrecorded deed does not protect the buyer against later purchasers or creditors who never heard of the sale.

Laurel County housing at a glance

London is the county seat and the largest city, and Corbin spreads over into Whitley and Knox counties. An estimated 63,746 people lived here in July 2025, up 1.8 percent from the 62,613 counted in 2020. The county has 27,063 housing units and 23,996 households, and owners live in 71.6 percent of occupied homes. The middle home value is $159,500 and the median rent is $813 a month. Alcohol sales are allowed only inside London city limits, which can matter to a buyer planning a commercial use.

How a deed must show where the seller got the property

Staff may turn away a deed that conveys a life estate or more unless it names where the seller's own title came from. KRS 382.110 sets the pattern for that reference.

  • Bought by recorded deed: cite the old deed's office, book, page and recording date.
  • Inherited, or acquired without a recorded writing: say how the title arrived and from whom.
  • Pieced together from more than one source: cite every source and mark which portion came from each.

Deeds signed by court commissioners or other court officers and instruments acknowledged before March 20, 1928 sit outside the rule. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it within 45 days of execution. A seller who inherited should locate the probate papers well before closing so the deed language is right the first time.

On a routine sale the clerk's own charges are one short deed and one short release, which is small beside the title and lender costs.

Kentucky deed transfer tax

The tax under KRS 142.050 is $0.50 for each $500 of declared value, and a partial $500 at the end counts as one more unit. The clerk computes it and holds the deed until it is paid.

If the deed is a gift or names only a token sum, the taxed value is the land's open market price. The clerk keeps five percent for collecting and sends the remainder to the county treasurer each quarter for the general fund. Several transfers owe nothing at all:

  • Foreclosure transfers and surrenders to a lender in place of foreclosure.
  • Spouse to spouse, or between ex-spouses in a divorce.
  • Token-price transfers down one or two generations.
  • Deeds that only create or release a debt security, or fix an earlier recorded deed.
  • Tax sale deeds and partitions.

Searching Laurel County land records

The clerk steers researchers to eCCLIX, an online index that lets title searchers, surveyors and agents view and print recorded documents from a desk. People without an account can come to the courthouse and look at the records on site. Accounts come through the vendor, Software Management, by mail, fax or email, with card payment after an invoice arrives.

Title firms that send closings electronically use one of four e-recording services posted by the clerk: Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. The closing agent's software picks among them, so the seller has nothing to choose.

Records stay free to read in person, and the online index is built for professionals who search many properties a month. A seller checking a single parcel before listing can simply ask the closing attorney or title agent to run the search.

Property tax bills to settle first

Property tax goes to the sheriff, not the clerk. The Laurel County Sheriff's Office, 1380 East Hwy 192 in London (606-864-6600), takes payment at the counter, by mailed check or at the drop box out front, and accepts cards inside on weekdays. KRS 134.015 sets the calendar: a full payment by November 1 saves 2 percent, the printed amount is due through year end, and late payers add 5 percent in January and 10 percent after that.

Bills unpaid at the April deadline become certificates of delinquency at the clerk's office, where interest and fees start accumulating. Outside buyers of those certificates register with the clerk each summer and post a deposit of 25 percent of their list value. Title agents want a payoff regardless, so request a bill history from the sheriff before listing.

  • Ask each lender for a payoff statement, and plan who files the release.
  • Provide the closing agent with the address where the buyer wants next year's bill sent.
  • Decide whether a transfer tax exemption applies and gather its supporting facts.

Owners who want no showings or repairs can get a direct cash offer, and the filing and tax steps above are the same whichever buyer signs.

What happens after the deed is signed

The signed deed goes to the clerk with the transfer tax and recording fee. The clerk holds the deed until the tax is paid, stamps it with the recording details, and sends the original back to whoever filed it, usually the closing attorney or title agent. Any mortgage payoff is released separately, so ask the lender who files the release and when to expect the recorded copy.

A cash sale does not change these steps, but it can shorten the wait, because there is no new lender package to assemble. Keep a copy of the recorded deed and the release with your sale papers. If a question comes up later about who owned the parcel on a given date, the clerk's records are where it gets settled.

With the Laurel County Clerk at 101 S Main St in London. That one office serves London and the Laurel County side of Corbin, since the deed goes where the land lies.

What does recording a Laurel County deed cost at minimum?

Fifty dollars buys five pages, and each extra page adds $3. A mortgage starts at $80 and a mortgage release at $46.

Yes. The grantor named in the deed owes it, and the clerk collects it at the counter when the deed comes in, at fifty cents per $500 of value.

Yes, in the clerk's office. Viewing from home through eCCLIX needs a paid account.

When must a lender file a deed in lieu of foreclosure?

Forty-five days after signing is the limit, and the filing goes to the clerk in the property's county. KRS 142.050 also leaves that deed free of transfer tax.

Where Fayette County deeds get recorded

Deeds go to the Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department, Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington. The phone number is 859-253-3344. The copy and inquiry counter stays open to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, yet recording ends at 4:00. A closing package that shows up at 4:15 sits until the next business day.

The clerk is a constitutional office, and its duties come from the Kentucky Revised Statutes. Besides recording, the office prepares property tax bills, runs elections and titles vehicles. Land records here go back to about 1792 and exist in books, on microfilm and as digital images.

For a seller, this office is where a sale ends. Once the deed is signed and the transfer tax is paid, recording puts the buyer's ownership on the public record. A closing agent normally walks the paperwork over, but the rules still matter when a deed is signed away from a title office.

Deed formatting rules

Since January 1, 2020, Kentucky clerks have followed the Property Records Industry Association layout standards for real estate documents, and the Fayette desk enforces them. Nonconforming paper can be refused on the spot. Check the layout before anyone signs.

  • Paper: 20 lb white stock with no watermarks, 8.5 by 11 inches preferred and 8.5 by 14 accepted, printed on one side only.
  • Margins: keep the top 3 inches of page one empty for the recorder's stamp and leave 1 inch elsewhere.
  • Text: type no smaller than 10-point Times New Roman or similar, at most nine lines per inch, in black ink with dark blue signatures.
  • No staples or binding, no colored highlighter marks and no embossed seals unless inked.

The desk records far more than deeds. The list includes deeds, quitclaim deeds, easements, powers of attorney, land contracts, affidavits of descent or heirship, mortgages, releases, lis pendens notices, judgment and mechanic's liens, and wills. A corrective deed or an affidavit of heirship goes through the same desk.

How to get a deed to the clerk

Over the counter, the office records weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Three other routes work too.

  • E-recording: the office accepts submissions through CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Hopdox, the channels title companies already use.
  • Mail or courier: send documents by US Mail, UPS or FedEx to Fayette County Clerk, 162 E. Main Street, Room 132, Lexington, KY 40507.
  • Drop box: a box in the Helix Garage, near the second-floor entrance to the clerk's office and to the right of the yellow garage fee kiosk, accepts envelopes weekdays between 7:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. The last pickup is at 4:00 p.m., and documents must be sealed in envelopes.

When mailing a deed, enclose payment for the recording fee and the transfer tax, or phone ahead for the exact total. A package that arrives underpaid holds up the closing.

Recording fees

Mail requests add $1.00 for postage and handling, and mailing a plat copy commonly costs $2.00. Copy requests by mail go on the clerk's form with payment, no more than two requests per form, and the office aims to fill them within three business days. The statute also lets the clerk collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent record storage on deeds, plats and mortgages. The window takes cash, credit cards or checks for copy fees.

Kentucky transfer tax on a Fayette sale

The seller, as grantor, owes it. The tax counts each $500 of declared value and rounds any partial block up. KRS 142.050 requires the county clerk to compute the tax and collect it before accepting the deed for recording. For a sale, value is the full price, liens included. For a gift, the clerk uses the estimated market price.

From each collection the clerk keeps 5 percent, then remits the rest each quarter to the county treasurer's general fund.

Transfers that escape the tax include divorce transfers between spouses, a parent or grandparent deeding to a child or grandchild for nominal consideration, foreclosure and deed-in-lieu transfers, delinquent tax sales, partitions, and deeds that only confirm or fix an earlier one. A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting is fined $50 per offense.

Searching land records and protecting your title

The clerk's online portal is fayettedeeds.com. Land records from 1970 to the present can be searched, viewed and printed there, and many earlier records sit in the non-indexed documents section. All plats have been digitized. Since January 3, 2022, the clerk has indexed documents exactly as written on the document instead of using its older abbreviation list, so try a few spelling variations when you search.

A free Recording Notification Service from the clerk sends an email when a document is filed against a name or address you register. Each email address can hold 10 items. It is sometimes called a fraud alert. The clerk cautions that it gives no guarantee of catching every filing.

  • Check the portal now and then for anything recorded in your name or against your property.
  • Look often at vacant property to be sure no one is occupying it unlawfully.
  • Give the PVA and the sheriff your correct mailing address so tax bills and notices reach you.
  • If fraud is suspected, call the Lexington Police Department at 859-258-3600 and a lawyer. The clerk cannot remove a recorded document without a court order.

Delinquent property taxes

The same office collects delinquent real property taxes once the sheriff passes them on after April 15. Payment must be cash, a money order, or a cashier's or certified check, and delinquent bills can be searched on fayettedeeds.com. A house sold with unpaid taxes needs the balance cleared before a clean deed can pass, so get a payoff figure early. The County Attorney, at 859-254-4941, arranges payment plans.

Selling a Fayette County house with title problems

Lexington and Fayette County run as one consolidated government, so the clerk alone handles recording for the whole city. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,636 a month in housing costs, owners without one pay $599, and renters pay $1,164.

A house in poor repair or with a title tangle can still stall on the open market. A closing held up by a late-found lien or a missing heir's affidavit can go smoother with a cash buyer who takes the property as-is while the title issue gets cleared at the recording desk. Record it with the Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department, Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington. You can walk it in, mail it, use the Helix Garage drop box or e-record through an approved vendor.

What time does the Fayette County Clerk stop recording documents?

Weekday recording ends at 4:00 p.m., though copy requests and questions are handled until 4:30 p.m. The drop box's last pickup is also 4:00 p.m.

What transfer tax applies to a Fayette County sale?

The seller pays $0.50 per $500 of value, and the clerk takes it before the deed goes on record.

Can I look up a Fayette County deed online?

Yes. Search fayettedeeds.com for land records from 1970 to the present, plus many older records in the non-indexed section. Plats are all online, and certified marriage records can be ordered there.

Does the Fayette County Clerk collect unpaid property taxes?

Yes, once the sheriff transfers a delinquent bill after April 15. Pay the clerk the full amount in cash, by money order, or with a cashier's or certified check. The County Attorney, at 859-254-4941, arranges payment plans.

Recordings office

The Recordings Department files the paper trail of land ownership in Madison County: deeds, mortgages, wills, plats and related documents. It operates from the Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave., Richmond, KY 40475, which opens its counter at 8 AM and closes at 4:30 PM. The recordings line is (859) 624-4703, extension 3.

The Berea Branch on Chestnut Street does motor vehicle work, dealer work, marriage licenses, voter registration and delinquent tax payments. Take recordings to Richmond. The clerk's home page carries a notice that the Richmond branch has relocated, so confirm the street address by phone before you carry an original deed across town.

Electronic submissions are worked each morning until roughly 9:30 to 10:00, and no wait-ons are offered then. Records reach back to 1786. Everything from 1986 onward is scanned for viewing at the counter or online through ECCLIX, a subscription service run by a third party. Searches work on a person's name only, so a street address will not find a deed.

What a Kentucky deed needs

KRS 382.135 spells out the contents and forbids a clerk from lodging a deed that fails them. The closing agent usually drafts the deed, but you can save a rejected filing by confirming spellings and mailing addresses.

  • The legal names of both parties, with a mailing address for each.
  • A statement of the price paid.
  • An address where the tax bill for the transfer year may be sent in care of someone.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the price shown is the whole price. On a gift or nominal sale, the certificate says so and puts an estimated fair cash value on the property.

A few deeds skip the price items: utility easements, transfers ordered in a divorce case, corrective deeds between the same parties, rights-of-way for government agencies, and cemetery lots. A swap of properties must state each property's fair cash value in the deed itself.

Real estate transfer tax

Sellers pay $0.50 per $500 slice of declared value, and a partial slice rounds up. KRS 142.050 makes the clerk do the arithmetic from the deed's stated value. No deed is accepted until the tax is paid, and the clerk stamps the payment date and amount on it. On a sale, value means the price plus any liens. On a gift or a token-price deed, value means what the property would fetch on the open market. Five percent of collections stays with the clerk as a handling fee, and the balance goes to the county treasurer each quarter.

  • Foreclosure transfers and deeds given in place of foreclosure owe nothing.
  • Neither do transfers between spouses or ex-spouses in a divorce, partitions, or sales for delinquent taxes.
  • Parent to child and grandparent to grandchild deeds with only nominal payment are exempt too.

Recording an inherited house

For a will, bring the original with the court order attached. The clerk records it, keeps the original, and charges the Will total on the fee schedule. When no will exists, an affidavit of descent under KRS 382.120 goes on record.

A separate duty falls on the personal representative. Before closing the estate, that person files an affidavit with the clerk in each county where the decedent held land, naming the people who receive each parcel and the full or estimated value of each. Heirs planning to sell should ask the probate lawyer whether that affidavit is on file, because a buyer's title examiner will look for it.

The clerk also runs DocAlert, a free email alert that tells you when a new deed or mortgage appears in your name. It matches only exact names, so a trust or a business should sign up under every spelling that might be recorded.

Unpaid property taxes

Once the bill reaches the clerk, extension 2 on the Richmond line handles questions. The clerk holds a yearly sale in the Fiscal Courtroom of the Courthouse Annex, 135 W. Irvine St., at 9 AM. Recording charges on a purchased lien are $30 for the assignment and $46 for a release.

The county bill funds the library, fiscal court, EMS, health department, school board and extension office. Some parcels also pay the Red Lick watershed district, the City of Richmond, the City of Berea or Berea Independent Schools.

Madison County is growing quickly. The 2025 estimate is 101,696 residents, a gain of 9.7 percent over April 2020, with owners living in 62 percent of homes. The median home value is $232,000 and median rent is $889.

Richmond is the county seat and the site of Eastern Kentucky University. Berea is home to Berea College. The county sits along I-75, with U.S. 25 and U.S. 421 as local routes, and Lexington is about 25 miles northwest of Richmond.

Because most recordings happen at closing, request the clerk's current charges and a transfer tax figure for your price before you sign. Bring a government photo ID, the signed deed, and the notarized price certificate to the counter, and ask the closing agent to say in advance who delivers the documents and who pays the clerk. At the Richmond Branch of the County Clerk, 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, before you go. The counter closes at 4:30 PM.

A half dollar per $500 of value, rounded up by block. The clerk collects it before taking the deed.

Yes. KRS 382.135 calls for a sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the stated price is the full price paid. A gift deed states that it is a gift and lists the estimated fair cash value.

Are Madison County land records searchable online?

Yes, through ECCLIX, a subscription service run by a third party, and every search uses a person's name. Documents from 1986 onward are scanned. Earlier ones are viewed at the Richmond office.

The grantor pays fifty cents on every $500 of value, counting a partial $500 as whole, before the deed is accepted (KRS 142.050). The clerk retains 5 percent as a collection fee, and the county treasurer receives the rest quarterly.

Corrective deeds, deeds that give or lift security for a debt, spouse transfers, foreclosure transfers and parent-to-child transfers for token money escape the tax. A gift is measured by what the house would sell for on the open market.

Inherited houses and liens

When a house comes down through a will or intestacy, the personal representative must file an affidavit with the clerk before the estate closes, naming each recipient and what the property is worth (KRS 382.135(4)). The clerk lists $50 for an affidavit of descent and $46 for a will.

Liens go on record at the same counter. Recording a certificate of delinquency costs $46, and so does its release. Unpaid property tax passes from the sheriff to the County Clerk after April 15, and a lien is recorded on the parcel. Judgment and mechanics' liens cost $46 in each direction. A parcel search at the clerk's counter before listing can head off surprises.

  • Find the deed book and page for your own title.

  • Request one total for recording fees and transfer tax.

Why each step matters: the deed book and page let the title agent find your chain of ownership quickly. The search for a lien, lis pendens or certificate shows whether a lawsuit or old tax debt is attached. The mailing address keeps the buyer's first bill from landing in the wrong mailbox, and the notary has to witness the sworn statement before the clerk will accept the deed. One quoted total for fees and tax lets you budget for closing without a surprise at the counter.

An heir with an empty Pendleton County house who would rather not make repairs can ask for a cash offer, and the buyer's closing agent then takes care of recording.

Planning the recording itself

Call 859-654-3380 and ask for one total on everything you plan to file, including the transfer tax, since fees vary by document type and a package that mixes types adds up. Bring the signed and notarized deed and the sworn statement of price. Know the mailing address where the buyer wants the first tax bill sent, because the clerk cannot file the deed without it.

If a lien or certificate turns up in a search, ask for a written payoff and the $46 release fee at the same visit, so the title is clean when the deed goes on record. Weekday hours are the surest bet. The second and last Saturday mornings are available too, but not on holiday weekends.

Other documents that come up in a sale

A few filings beyond the deed show up in sales and estates. A power of attorney costs $50 to record, which matters when someone signs for an owner who cannot be at closing. A plat is $50. A mortgage runs $80, and one that includes an assignment runs $126. A deed that carries a release inside it is $96, against $50 for a plain deed, so combining documents can change the bill.

Judgment liens, releases and a certificate of delinquency are each $46. Each old filing therefore carries its own recording cost, on top of whatever debt sits behind it. Ask the clerk for the full list of what is recorded against the parcel before you set a closing date.

When the owner has died

For an estate, the personal representative files an affidavit listing each heir and the value of the property before the estate closes. The affidavit of descent costs $50, and recording a will costs $46. Heirs who live out of town should line up a notary and decide on one mailing address for the first tax bill before the deed is signed.

Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4 p.m., and on the second and last Saturday of each month until noon, barring a holiday weekend.

What does recording a Pendleton County deed cost?

The clerk lists $50 for a plain deed, $96 when a release is included and $46 when the deed is exempt from the state fee.

Who pays transfer tax on a Pendleton County sale?

The seller, as grantor, at fifty cents per $500 of value with a partial $500 counted whole. The clerk collects it before accepting the deed.

What does it cost to record a lien release in Pendleton County?

$46 for a release of a lien or mortgage, and the same for recording a certificate of delinquency.

Where can I get a certified copy of my deed?

At the Pendleton County Clerk in Falmouth, which charges $5 for a certified copy and $2 for a standard one.

The Legal Records Division of the Jefferson County Clerk's office is the official repository for deeds, mortgages, releases and liens on Louisville real estate. Until your deed is taxed, accepted and indexed there, the sale doesn't show on the public record.

The Deed Room works out of Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204, Louisville, KY 40202, telephone 502-574-6220. Tax collection after April 15 sits at a different counter, Suite 100a in the same building.

The office runs a free alert service called ClerkAlert. It emails owners whenever a paper is filed under their name or business name, and some sellers keep it switched on after closing as a guard against forged deeds or surprise liens.

Recording fees

Look for the charge on your settlement statement as its own line, apart from the recording fee.

Some transfers pay nothing. The ones sellers meet most often are these:

  • A deed that only secures or releases a debt.
  • A corrective deed that confirms one already on record.

Why the Clerk turns a deed away

Unpaid property tax and the Clerk

At the close of business on April 15, any current-year bill still open leaves the Sheriff and lands with the Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. By then the Sheriff's schedule has added a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent add-on fee, and the Clerk's side starts adding interest at 1 percent per month.

The PVA's count of 83 taxing jurisdictions includes about 60,000 properties in the smaller home rule cities, many of which send their own bill. Recording works the same across all of them, but a seller in a small city should check for a city tax balance before closing.

Preparing for the closing day filing

The closing agent normally files for the buyer, and the office also takes electronic filings. Still, the paperwork starts with you. Sign the deed before a notary, confirm the preparation statement is signed, and give the agent the book and page of your own title so it can be cited.

Charged to you as grantor. KRS 142.050 imposes it on the seller named in the deed. Transfers such as those between spouses or through foreclosure are exempt when the deed cites the exemption.

Typical causes are a missing preparation statement, no source of title, no stated market value, no tax-bill mailing address, a weak notary block or the wrong fee. An LLC seller also has to be registered with the Secretary of State first.

How recording works step by step

The closing agent brings the signed, notarized deed and the consideration statement to the clerk, or sends them through one of the e-recording vendors. Is online deed searching free in Letcher County?

For residents researching personal matters, yes, up to five searches a day in Letcher County records. Commercial researchers pay a subscription.

Does a house gift to a child owe transfer tax?

No, when the price is nominal and the deed runs from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which KRS 142.050 exempts. A gift deed to anyone else is taxed on open market value.

The buyer may sue to foreclose one year after the certificate is created. The property carries a lien until the bill is paid in full, so if you see an unpaid year in your file, clear it before a buyer's title company finds it.

Anyone who buys the bill must follow KRS 134.490, KRS 134.546 and the rest of Chapter 134. If you pay such a buyer, ask the clerk at Suite 206 for a copy of the recorded release for a small fee. Give it to the title company.

What the Webster County Clerk's office in Dixon handles

The same office licenses vehicles, runs elections, issues notary bonds, and processes delinquent real estate taxes. For someone selling a house it matters three times: when the buyer's deed is recorded, when a paid-off mortgage needs its release put on the record, and when a bill misses the Sheriff's April 15 cutoff and lands at the Clerk with a lien attached.

Land records here reach back to 1786, though the county itself dates from 1860. Disputes about records or fines go to the courts, at 270-639-9160 or 270-639-9300.

Records you can search online

All of them are free to view, a service that began August 1, 2010. Staff are still scanning and indexing older books, so coverage keeps growing. Here is what can be viewed:

  • Deeds: every book from 1860 (Book 1) forward, plus deeds of partition for 1893 through 2017.

  • Plats, all current ones, with the oldest in the two Processioner books covering 1861 to 1912.
  • Wills and marriage records from 1860, and every fixture filing.

A link beside the land records leads to a delinquent tax lookup. Before listing, search your name in the index and confirm each paid mortgage shows a release. Then check for liens, lis pendens notices, and judgments, because a title examiner who finds an unreleased one late in the process can push a closing back.

Deed formatting rules

Since January 1, 2020, Webster County has followed the Property Records Industry Association layout rules, as every Kentucky county clerk does. A document that ignores them can be rejected at the window.

  • White 20 lb paper, 8 1/2 by 11 preferred and 8 1/2 by 14 accepted, with no watermarks.
  • One-sided printing, no staples or binding, no raised seals, no highlighter.
  • Leave 3 inches clear at the top of page one for the recorder, with 1 inch margins everywhere else.
  • Black ink with dark blue signatures, 10-point Times New Roman or similar, at most 9 lines per inch.

A closing attorney usually deals with this, so most sellers never see the rules. Trouble comes mainly when a family transfer is typed up from a template.

The seller pays Kentucky 50 cents per $500 of value, and any leftover partial block is rounded up. The rule sits in KRS 142.050. The Clerk figures it from the deed, takes payment up front, and stamps the date and amount onto the deed.

KRS 382.110 sets two clocks. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must record it within 45 days of signing. A person receiving a deed from a court-appointed commissioner gets five business days. Other filings arrive too: a mortgage release to clear the old loan, an affidavit of descent that records who inherited, and releases of mechanic liens or lis pendens notices that otherwise cloud the title. Deeds for Anderson County land are recorded at the County Clerk's counter, 100 S Main St, Lawrenceburg, KY 40342. Recording is what protects the buyer against later purchasers who had no notice and against the seller's creditors (KRS 382.110(1)).

Lawrenceburg is the seat and the only city. Most sellers never walk the deed in themselves. What must be written into the deed

KRS 382.135 bars the clerk from accepting a deed that leaves out certain items. A quick review before the closing saves a second trip.

  • A statement of the entire consideration.

KRS 382.110 adds a title-source rule. The deed names the earlier deed by office, book, page and recording date, or explains how the seller acquired the land if it came through inheritance. When a house passed under a will, or with none, an affidavit from the estate's personal representative is also needed. It is filed before the estate closes and names each person who received property, each parcel and its value.

Recording fees at the clerk

How the state transfer tax works

The seller pays $0.50 for each $500 of value stated in the deed, and a leftover partial $500 counts as a whole one (KRS 142.050). A gift, or a deed that recites only token consideration, is taxed on open-market value. Some transfers owe nothing:

To claim an exemption, use the Exempt Transfer Affidavit, Form 71A245, which is on the clerk's records page.

The same office renews vehicle registrations. Online renewal asks for a title number, a plate number and a credit card, and a VIN lookup shows the prior year's vehicle tax. Voter registration and election results belong to the elections department.

Forms are grouped as motor vehicle, legal records, elections and delinquent tax. Sellers mostly need the legal records group, which includes the Exempt Transfer Affidavit, a release of a real estate mortgage, a release of a vendor's lien and an affidavit of conversion to real estate.

  • Get this year's bill and any older balance from the Sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk about any recorded lien or lis pendens.
  • Write in the buyer's mailing address for the tax bill.
  • Prepare the exemption affidavit if one applies.

If the house came to you by inheritance, add two items: the affidavit from the estate's personal representative and, when the land passed by descent, the affidavit of descent, which the clerk lists at a $50 minimum. Bring a checkbook or ask the closing office how it will pay, because the clerk holds the deed until the fees and the transfer tax are paid.

The county's population is estimated at 25,225 in mid-2025, up from 23,852 in 2020. It touches seven other counties and belongs to the Frankfort micropolitan area. Deeds for Grayson County land are recorded at the Grayson County Clerk's office, 125 East Market Street, Leitchfield, KY 42754. KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the clerk of whichever county contains the land, or most of it. Recording is what makes the deed stand up against later buyers and creditors who never saw it.

Two numbers matter for property work. Recording and delinquent taxes are at (270) 259-5295. The licensing and transfers desk is at (270) 259-3201. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:00 and opens the second Saturday of each month from 8:00 to 11:00. If your closing is set for a specific day, call ahead and confirm the office will be open.

Land in Leitchfield, Caneyville, Clarkson, Big Clifty or out near the lakes is all filed in this one office. The Clerk's website has an online records section where you can look up older instruments, which helps when you need the deed that put the current owner on title.

Kentucky transfer tax on a sale

Kentucky charges fifty cents on every $500 of price, rounding a leftover partial block up. Responsibility falls on the seller. When the deed is handed in, the Clerk does the math. Nothing gets recorded until the Clerk has the money, so bring it to closing.

For a gift, or a deed that recites only nominal money, the value used is what the property would bring on the open market. Liens on the property count toward the value of a sale. One transaction is taxed once. Of what the Clerk collects, 5 percent covers the office's handling and the remainder goes to the county treasurer's general fund.

Ask the Clerk's recording desk for the exact figure before closing day so the seller's net sheet is right and the title company has a number to put on the settlement statement.

Transfers that skip the tax

The statute exempts many transfers. Ordinary homeowners tend to run into these:

  • a deed that only pledges property for a debt, or lifts that pledge;
  • a correction deed, or a confirmation of one already of record;
  • a deed from one spouse to the other, including ex-spouses dividing property in a divorce;
  • a foreclosure, or an owner handing the house back to the lender to avoid one;
  • a sale for unpaid taxes or assessments, and a partition among co-owners;
  • a token-price deed from a parent to a child or a grandparent to a grandchild.

A transfer into a trust is also free of the tax when the grantor is the only beneficiary. A clerk who willfully records a taxable deed without collecting can be fined $50 per offense, so expect the Clerk's staff to look closely at the price or value stated on your deed.

Tracing the owner's title in the deed

Each deed must point back to how the seller came to own the land. If an earlier deed was recorded, the new deed cites its office, book, page and recording date. If the land came by inheritance or another unrecorded route, the deed explains how and from whom the grantor took title.

If the parcel was pieced together from several sources, the deed names each one and marks the portion that came from each. Clerks are barred from accepting a deed that omits the trail. Deeds from court commissioners, sheriffs and other court officers acting in that role are outside the rule.

When a house has stayed in one family, the earlier deed may be decades old, and the book and page reference is the only link a title examiner can follow back. Before anyone drafts the new deed, pull the last deed that vested title in the current owner. A wrong book and page cite sends the paper back to whoever prepared it, which can delay a closing.

Unpaid property tax and the Clerk

An unpaid bill leaves the sheriff at closing time on April 15 and goes to the Clerk, who records a lien. Each month, or part of one, adds one percent interest, and both the Clerk and the county attorney charge a commission on top. A sale of the tax certificate can be scheduled from day 90 to day 135 after the transfer, and an outside buyer at that sale adds costs of their own.

Because the lien attaches to the parcel, any title search the buyer orders will turn it up. If you are selling, call the Clerk's delinquent tax line at (270) 259-5295 and ask for an exact payoff before the closing date. Usually the payoff comes out of the seller's proceeds at the closing table.

What to bring when you record

Treat the Clerk's counter as the last stop before the sale is public record. The title company or attorney usually carries the paperwork over, but a seller handling things directly should have the signed deed, the money for the transfer tax and the recording fee, and a copy of the earlier deed showing how the grantor got title. If a mortgage is being paid off, the release should be on its way to the same office.

Here is how a typical closing flows. Back taxes get paid off, the deed is signed, the Clerk works out the transfer tax, and the deed is then recorded and indexed. Once it is indexed, the buyer's name replaces yours in the public record.

A quick cash sale avoids a lender's conditions, yet the filing steps do not change. The deed still has to cite the prior title, and the tax still has to be paid before the Clerk accepts it.

Frequently asked questions

What is the address of the Grayson County Clerk?

125 East Market Street, Leitchfield, KY 42754. For recording and delinquent tax questions call (270) 259-5295. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:00.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Grayson County house sale?

The seller. The rate is fifty cents per $500 of value, and the Clerk collects it before the deed is recorded.

Does a deed in lieu of foreclosure carry the transfer tax?

No, KRS 142.050 excuses that transfer. The lender must still record the deed within 45 days of signing it.

What if my deed leaves out how I got title?

The Clerk cannot accept it. The deed must cite the earlier recorded deed by book and page, or explain how title arrived by inheritance or other unrecorded means.

Do old property taxes get paid when a Grayson County house sells?

Yes, normally at closing, since the lien stays on the parcel. Get a payoff quote from the Clerk's delinquent tax line first.
